title: Talking about a film or a book
why: This lesson opens the unit on culture and leisure: you learn to summarize a movie, a series or a book in the narrative present and to give your opinion with precise adjectives. It reuses the past tenses, relatives and connectors of earlier units in one of the most common conversations in France.

What's it about?

Telling a friend about a film, a series or a book is one of the most natural conversations there is. It needs a few key phrases, and one tense you already know: the present. As in English, a summary is told in the present, even if the story is set in the past. This is called the narrative present.

FrenchEnglish
Ça parle de…It's about…
C'est l'histoire de…It's the story of…
L'histoire se passe à Paris / en Bretagne / dans les années 1960.The story takes place in Paris / in Brittany / in the 1960s.
Le personnage principal, c'est…The main character is…
C'est un film de… / un roman de…It's a film by… / a novel by…
C'est l'histoire d'une jeune femme qui quitte Lille et part vivre à Nice. Là-bas, elle rencontre un vieux pêcheur et tout change.It's the story of a young woman who leaves Lille and goes to live in Nice. There, she meets an old fisherman and everything changes.

Genres

une comédie, un drame, un film policier (in speech, un polar), un film d'animation, un documentaire, une série, un roman, une BD (bande dessinée, comics, hugely popular in France and Belgium).

False friends: un roman is a novel, not a romance (that's une histoire d'amour). Une nouvelle is a short story, not a novel. And the person who directs a film is le réalisateur or la réalisatrice; un directeur runs a company or a school.

", "

What did you think?

The most natural way to give your impression is j'ai trouvé ça + adjective. Ça has no gender, so the adjective stays masculine singular: J'ai trouvé ça génial. If you use an object pronoun instead, the participle and the adjective agree with the film, the series or the book:

Le film ? Je l'ai trouvé émouvant. / La série ? Je l'ai trouvée drôle.The movie? I found it moving. / The series? I found it funny.
AdjectiveEnglish
passionnant / passionnantegripping, fascinating
émouvant / émouvantemoving, touching
bouleversant / bouleversantedeeply moving, overwhelming
drôlefunny
ennuyeux / ennuyeuseboring
décevant / décevantedisappointing
lent / lenteslow

Careful with two traps. Décevant means disappointing, never \"deceiving\". And to say a film is exciting, choose passionnant: excitant can sound sexual or simply odd.

Recommending (or not)

Je le recommande / Je te le conseille (I recommend it), Ça vaut le coup (it's worth it), À voir absolument ! (a must-see), La fin est surprenante (the ending is surprising). And when you didn't get into it: Je n'ai pas accroché (informal).

Don't give away the ending! Say Je ne te raconte pas la fin (I won't tell you the ending).

", "

Going to the movies in France

The French love cinema: there are movie theaters even in small towns, and Paris offers one of the widest choices of films in the world. A few words to get by:

FrenchEnglish
la séance de 20 hthe 8 p.m. showing
en VO (version originale) sous-titréein the original language, with subtitles
en VF (version française)dubbed into French
la bande-annoncethe trailer
l'acteur / l'actricethe actor / the actress
l'auteur / l'autricethe author, the writer

French cinema is famous for its comedies, its family dramas and its films d'auteur, where the director's personal style comes first. Each year, the Cannes festival and the César awards are big events.

Putting it all together

J'ai vu un film italien en VO. Ça parle d'un vieux musicien qui retourne dans son village. J'ai trouvé ça très beau, mais un peu lent. Je te le recommande quand même !I saw an Italian movie in the original version. It's about an old musician who goes back to his village. I found it very beautiful, but a bit slow. I recommend it anyway!

You'll also hear l'auteure, a feminine form that started in Quebec. Both autrice and auteure are used in France today.
